title: Port To Port
description: Trace one shipment's entire journey from booking to delivery and prove the database's status/timestamp story is internally consistent at every single step, not just at the start and the end.
successCondition: Book a shipment, then repeatedly call POST /api/tracking/:id/advance, querying the full shipments row via `npm run db:psql` after each call, until status reaches "delivered". Confirm: (1) status transitions in the exact order booked -> in_transit -> ... -> delivered with no skipped or repeated backward transitions, (2) position_updated_at is non-decreasing across every single tick, (3) current_lat/current_lng at the final "delivered" tick exactly equal destination_lat/destination_lng, and (4) created_at never changes across any of the ticks — only positional/status fields mutate.
hints: Keep a running log of the full row (not just status) after each /advance call — this challenge is about the whole lifecycle's consistency, not just the final state.
The number of ticks needed to reach "delivered" depends on the origin/destination distance — a short in-city-ish route reaches delivered in fewer calls if you want to keep the test shorter.
